elements.name: Parent User
elements.rationale: Role checks and frontend/backend route bindings show the system explicitly recognizes and serves a parent role interacting with multiple API services.

elements.name: Child User
elements.rationale: Role checks and route bindings show the system explicitly recognizes a child role that logs in and accesses child-oriented video/profile features.

elements.name: Administrator
elements.rationale: Admin-only role checks on user management routes indicate a distinct administrator actor outside the system boundary.

elements.name: Authentication Service
elements.rationale: The auth router is mounted as one coherent backend service handling registration, login, identity lookup, and password change with reads/writes to user and child profile data.

elements.name: Child Profile Service
elements.rationale: The children router is mounted as one coherent service for child profiles, approvals, and search/watch history, with sustained reads/writes to child profile and video records.

elements.name: Video Management Service
elements.rationale: The videos router is a single service that uploads, lists, streams, updates, deletes, likes, and comments on videos while reading/writing video records.

elements.name: User Profile and Administration Service
elements.rationale: The users router is one service for profile retrieval/update, aggregate stats, and admin user management backed by user, child profile, and video data access.

elements.name: Image Upload Handler
elements.rationale: A shared upload middleware handles multipart image uploads for profile and child ID images and writes files to the server filesystem.

elements.name: Static Upload Delivery
elements.rationale: The server mounts a static file handler exposing uploaded files from the uploads directory.
elements.uncertainty_note: Only the static mount is directly evidenced; the implementation details of any additional processing are not shown in the facts.

elements.name: User Accounts Database
elements.rationale: The code defines a persisted Mongoose model mapped to the users MongoDB collection.

elements.name: Child Profiles Database
elements.rationale: The code defines a persisted Mongoose model mapped to the childprofiles MongoDB collection.

elements.name: Videos Database
elements.rationale: The code defines a persisted Mongoose model mapped to the videos MongoDB collection.

elements.name: Uploaded Images File Store
elements.rationale: Image upload middleware stores uploaded image files in a persistent server-side directory.

elements.name: Uploaded Videos File Store
elements.rationale: Video uploads and static serving both point to the backend uploads directory as a persistent file store for uploaded media.
elements.uncertainty_note: The facts show a shared uploads area and a video uploader rooted at backend/uploads; they do not fully separate video files from other uploaded content at the storage level.

elements.name: Browser Local Storage
elements.rationale: Frontend code reads and writes token, user, and cookie-banner values in browser localStorage, making it a client-side persistent data store.

Age-check middleware reads a user account by id during protected processing that uses age verification.

Authentication-related frontend logic writes token and user session data into browser local storage after login/registration/profile refresh.
flows.uncertainty_note: These facts evidence localStorage writes in AuthContext; mapping them to the Authentication Service is an architectural grouping choice across frontend auth/session handling.

flows.description: Authentication-related frontend logic reads stored token and user session data from browser local storage.
flows.uncertainty_note: Facts show AuthContext and API config reading token/user from localStorage; mapped to Authentication Service as the auth/session process.

flows.description: Authentication-related frontend logic removes token and user session data from browser local storage during logout/session cleanup.
